name: RestGPT: Connecting Large Language Models with Real-World RESTful APIs
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2306.06624, cs.CL). Submitted 11 Jun 2023 (v1), last revised 27 Aug 2023 (v2, which adds RestBench). DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2306.06624. No peer-reviewed conference/journal venue identified; it remains an arXiv preprint.
authors_affiliation: Yifan Song, Weimin Xiong, Dawei Zhu, Wenhao Wu, Han Qian, Mingbo Song, Hailiang Huang (Peking University), Cheng Li, Ke Wang, Rong Yao, Ye Tian (Huawei Technologies), Sujian Li (Peking University, corresponding author). Primary affiliation: School of Computer Science, Peking University (PKU-TANGENT lab), with Huawei Technologies. {yfsong, lisujian}@pku.edu.cn.
code_url: https://github.com/Yifan-Song793/RestGPT (MIT license; project page https://restgpt.github.io/). Built on LangChain; prompts inspired by the LangChain OpenAPI agent.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Yifan-Song793/RestGPT (1.4k stars, 16 commits, last meaningful commit 2023; not a continuously-updated leaderboard. Also hosts the RestBench datasets under /datasets and OAS specs under /specs).
task_domain: tool-use (LLM agent calling real-world RESTful APIs) with strong planning/decision-making component; touches web-service control and code (the parser generates Python parsing code). Builds an autonomous agent that controls real-world applications (movie database, music player) via RESTful APIs.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, online (test-time) tool-use: given a complex natural-language user instruction, the agent must decompose it into sub-tasks and select/execute the correct sequence of real RESTful API endpoints (which follow the OpenAPI Specification / Swagger and return JSON), parsing responses to feed the next step. Closed-source LLMs (text-davinci-003 primary; also ChatGPT, Llama2-13B, Vicuna-13B) are used purely via prompting with in-context examples; no training/fine-tuning of the LLM or any retriever. The agent interacts with LIVE APIs (TMDB movie database, Spotify music player), so it must be robust to real API feedback, errors, and unforeseen situations. Supervision: none for the model; evaluation uses human-annotated gold API solution paths. The challenge is API understanding under a limited context window (cannot fit all API docs), planning under inter-API dependencies, parameter formulation, and parsing lengthy/complex JSON responses.
what_is_retrieved: tools / docs: real-world RESTful API endpoints and their OpenAPI Specification (OAS) documentation. The API Selector 'retrieves' (selects) which endpoint(s) to call for the current sub-task by reading endpoint names+descriptions of all available APIs; the Caller then loads the full detailed OAS doc of the chosen endpoint(s); the Parser reads the OAS response schema.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed set of real-world RESTful API endpoints described by their OpenAPI Specification (TMDB 54 / Spotify 40 endpoints in RestBench v2). The store of API documentation is external and static (not an agent-written growing episodic memory); selection/retrieval is performed online over this fixed API set.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness of a minimal multi-API solution path rather than a fixed top-k ranking: the goal across a full instruction is to recover the complete (minimal) sequence of API endpoints (the gold solution path, scored by Correct Path rate as a subsequence match). At each individual step the API selector picks the needed API(s) (one or a few) for the current sub-task; there is no fixed-k retrieved set and no precision/recall@k ranking objective. The headline objective is end-to-end task completion via the correct ordered set of APIs.
retrieval_unit: tool-API endpoint (a single RESTful API endpoint, e.g. GET /movie/{movie_id}/credits) is the retrievable/selectable unit. Its associated documentation is the OAS entry (API path, description, request method, parameter list, response schema, response example, errors). The API selector keys on endpoint name + description; the caller then consumes the full per-endpoint OAS document.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-curated: the authors filter the official OAS of each application down to a fixed set of commonly-used endpoints (TMDB 54, Spotify 40 in RestBench v2; v1 used the full 135 TMDB / 71 Spotify endpoints). The retrievable store of API endpoints/docs is built once and does not grow at test time. The underlying applications are live (real API calls return real, changing data), but the API index itself is static.
index_structure_topology: Flat per-endpoint document set keyed by endpoint name and natural-language description (the API selector is shown the names and descriptions of all available endpoints). Within each endpoint the OAS is structured (path, parameters, response schema). The framework imposes a CONTENT-SEPARATION / progressive-disclosure structure across modules rather than a graph or hierarchy: the API selector sees only short endpoint descriptions, while the caller loads the full doc and the parser loads the response schema on demand. No explicit dependency graph or category hierarchy is used for selection. [uncertain] whether any embedding/vector index is used (the paper describes the selector as an LLM reading all endpoint descriptions, implying no separate vector retriever for the 54/40-endpoint sets).
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever: API selection is done by an LLM (the API Selector module) that reads the endpoint names and descriptions of all available APIs and chooses the appropriate endpoint(s) for the current natural-language sub-task. It is NOT a BM25/dense/learned embedding retriever; no trained retrieval model is used. Table 1 of the paper marks its API use as 'API selection with retrieval' but the realized mechanism is prompted-LLM selection over the full API-description list.
retriever_learning_signal: none: the API selector LLM is used off-the-shelf via prompting with a few in-context examples; there is no contrastive training, no LM-feedback fine-tuning, no RL, and no learned retrieval policy. Selection quality comes entirely from the frozen LLM's text comprehension of endpoint descriptions plus the coarse-to-fine prompt design.
query_construction: Two-level, thought-conditioned: (1) the Planner produces a high-level natural-language sub-task p_t conditioned on the user query q and the history of prior NL plans and execution results (p_1,r_1,...,p_{t-1},r_{t-1}); (2) this NL sub-task is used as the query to the API Selector, which maps it to a finer API calling plan a_t (conditioned also on prior execution results / background such as resolved ids). No embedding query vector is built; the 'query' is the natural-language sub-task plus accumulated background context.
query_granularity: step/sub-task level (online, per iteration) and effectively two-level: a coarse NL sub-task query (planner) refined into a finer API-selection query (API selector). Retrieval/selection happens once per planning step within the iterative plan-and-execute loop, not once at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: iterative (online): API selection occurs at every planning step in the coarse-to-fine online plan-and-execute loop until the planner emits an 'end' signal. The planner can also emit a 'continue' signal that triggers re-selection of a new API plan for the same sub-task based on the latest execution result. Selection is thus interleaved with execution rather than one-shot.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent/planner-driven schedule: retrieval (API selection) is triggered each step by the planner generating a new NL sub-task; a special 'continue' signal (planner judging the current executor output has not fulfilled the sub-task) re-triggers selection of a new API plan, and an 'end' signal terminates the loop. The trigger is the planner's LLM-judged progress/feedback state, not a token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, or reflection-token mechanism.
reranking: None. The API selector directly chooses the endpoint(s) for the sub-task; there is no separate reranking stage (no cross-encoder, RRF, or hierarchy-aware reranker). [uncertain] whether the selector internally weighs multiple candidates beyond the LLM's selection.
retrieved_context_refinement: Progressive disclosure / content separation plus response distillation: (1) only the chosen endpoint's full OAS document is loaded for the caller (docs for non-selected APIs are filtered out to fit the context window); (2) the Parser generates Python code from the OAS response schema to extract just the required fields from lengthy JSON responses (with a direct-LLM-parse backup if the code errors), distilling the API response into a short natural-language execution result returned to the planner. This is decompose-then-load and reason-in-response-schema distillation rather than rerank/compress of retrieved candidates.
tool_document_engineering: API/tool descriptions are taken from the OpenAPI Specification (OAS / Swagger) and split by field across modules: the API selector consumes endpoint names + short descriptions, the caller consumes the full per-endpoint doc (path, parameters, request body), and the parser consumes the response schema. The authors curate/filter the official OAS to a commonly-used subset, but do not perform synthetic-query augmentation, summary expansion, weighted-field embeddings, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings; documentation is used largely as-is (raw OAS) and routed by field.
index_content_separation: Yes, central design: a lightweight retrievable index (endpoint names + descriptions seen by the API selector) is separated from heavy content loaded on demand (the caller loads the full OAS doc only for endpoints in the current API plan; the parser loads the response schema). This OAS-field-routed progressive disclosure is explicitly motivated by the limited LLM context window so the framework can scale to 100+ APIs.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Integration protocol is RESTful (HTTP GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH over URIs, via the Python Requests library), with API definitions standardized through the OpenAPI Specification (OAS/Swagger). This enables plug-and-play connection to any RESTful application. The API index is static per scenario (curated OAS subset); there is no automatic live CRUD synchronization of the index, no RapidAPI integration, and no MCP (predates MCP).
tool_dependency_awareness: Implicit/handled by online planning rather than an explicit dependency model: inter-API dependencies (e.g., output id of one call feeding the in-path parameter of the next, such as getting a user_id before creating a playlist for that user) are resolved by the iterative coarse-to-fine planner+executor passing accumulated 'background' results forward. The paper's case study highlights that offline/ReAct baselines fail precisely because they ignore such dependencies, whereas RestGPT's online planning respects them. There is NO explicit dependency graph, bipartite KG, or dependency-aware reranker; dependencies are managed via context/state carried across steps.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation within an agentic plan-and-execute loop: the selected endpoint's OAS documentation grounds the Caller's prompt to formulate correct parameters/request body and call the live API; the response schema grounds the Parser's code generation; the distilled execution result is fed back to the Planner as natural-language context to plan the next step. No training signal and no latent-token injection; retrieval is used purely as in-context grounding.
planning_integration: retrieve(select)-then-execute interleaved per step inside an iterative coarse-to-fine online planning loop: Planner generates a coarse NL sub-task -> API Selector maps it to a finer API plan (the selection step) -> Executor (Caller+Parser) calls the API and returns a parsed result -> Planner re-plans the next sub-task online from feedback. 'Continue'/'end' control signals govern re-selection and termination. Not a one-shot exemplar, MCTS/tree search, or plan-then-execute offline scheme; it is a per-step coarse-to-fine plan/select/act/feedback loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-sub-task / per-planning-step (which corresponds to per-tool-call or per-few-tool-calls within the rollout): API selection and execution are interleaved with the planner's reasoning at each step, with possible intra-sub-task re-selection on a 'continue' signal. Coarser than per-token; finer than per-answer.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning). The closest analogue is execution-feedback-driven online re-planning: when an API call result is judged insufficient, the planner issues 'continue' and the API selector regenerates the API plan from the latest feedback. This adapts the PLAN, not a retrieved prior case.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw OpenAPI Specification documentation injected as prompt context: endpoint name+description (for selection), full endpoint doc with parameters and request body (for the caller), and response schema (for the parser). Surface form is structured/raw API documentation text, not a distilled strategy, free-text workflow, executable skill, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw documentation of a concrete tool: each retrieved/selected unit is a single concrete API endpoint and its specification (a tool spec), not a distilled strategy, state-aware guideline, reusable workflow, procedural skill, or demonstration.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Coarse-to-fine online planning with execution feedback provides robustness: dividing planning (planner) from API selection (selector) lets the LLM handle one of API-understanding/selection/planning at a time; the planner monitors executor output via 'continue'/'end' signals to recover from incomplete/erroneous results; the parser has a direct-LLM-parse fallback when generated parsing code errors. The paper demonstrates robustness to NOISE APIs (adding distractor/noise endpoints from official TMDB barely degrades RestGPT while baselines deteriorate). No retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator, or distractor-aware SFT (everything is prompting-based).
memory_type: none (no persistent learned memory). The system carries within-episode working context (prior NL plans p_1..p_{t-1} and execution results r_1..r_{t-1}) across steps to enable online planning, but this is transient per-instruction context, not an episodic store, skill library, workflow memory, graph, or latent memory that persists across tasks.
write_back: false: RestGPT does not write new experiences, cases, or skills into any persistent memory. Each instruction is solved fresh; nothing learned from one instruction is stored for future instructions. (Note: a baseline, Reflexion, does maintain reflective episodic memory across trials, but RestGPT itself does not.)
online_growth: false: the retrievable store (curated set of RESTful API endpoints / OAS docs) is fixed per scenario and does not grow during deployment. The agent does not add new tools, cases, or skills to its store at test time.
write_back_trigger: never: there is no memory write-back mechanism. The only persistence within an episode is the running plan/result history used as context for the next planning step, which is discarded after the instruction completes.
failure_experience_usage: N/A / none: failed API calls or wrong plans are handled within the current episode via online re-planning ('continue' signal) and the parser's fallback, but no failure (or success) experiences are stored or later retrieved. There is no success-only vs success+failure memory; nothing is retained across instructions.
memory_evolution_update: N/A: no stored memory entries exist to mutate. Within an episode the context is append-only (each step's plan and result is appended to the running history), but there is no cross-episode memory to update, dedup, refine, or prune.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: API selection is a frozen prompted-LLM decision, not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval or case-selection policy. There is no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, value function, or trained ranker; selection is LLM-as-retriever over endpoint descriptions.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent system with private within-episode context; no memory or experience sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks. (RestGPT is itself plug-and-play across RESTful applications, but that is tool/API portability, not shared experience.)
benchmarks: RestBench (introduced by this paper): two real-world scenarios - TMDB movie database (54 commonly-used API endpoints; 100 test instructions; gold solution-path lengths 1-4, avg 2.3) and Spotify music player (40 endpoints; 57 test instructions; lengths 1-4, avg 2.6), each with 10 development instructions. Human-annotated instructions with gold API solution paths. (Paper v1 reported the full OAS scale of 135 TMDB / 71 Spotify endpoints; v2 RestBench uses the filtered 54 / 40 subsets.) Plus an auxiliary noise-API scaling experiment: 10 hand-picked TMDB APIs + 15 instructions, with increasing numbers of added noise APIs.
benchmark_family: tool (tool/API-use agent benchmark over real RESTful APIs). RestBench is a real-application RESTful-API tool-use benchmark with human-annotated gold solution paths, distinct from synthetic tool benchmarks; it is an early member of the tool-use benchmark family alongside API-Bank and ToolBench/ToolLLM.
baselines: Four planning/tool baselines, all equipped with RestGPT's proposed API executor for fair comparison and all run with text-davinci-003: (1) Offline introspective method (plan-then-execute, as in HuggingGPT/Chameleon); (2) DEPS (Describe, Explain, Plan and Select; max 10 steps); (3) ReAct (interleaved reasoning+acting); (4) Reflexion (verbal reflection in episodic memory, max 2 trials). Plus internal ablations (w/o Planner = ReAct + executor; w/o Parser) and base-LLM variants (ChatGPT/gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, Llama2-13B-chat, Vicuna-13B-v1.5).
key_metrics: Success Rate (%, human-judged whether the result fulfills the query), Correct Path rate (CP, %; model's API-call path contains the gold path as a subsequence), and Delta Solution Length (mean number of EXTRA API calls beyond gold for successfully completed instructions; lower/closer-to-0 is better, measures planning efficiency).
headline_result: On RestBench with text-davinci-003, RestGPT achieves 75.0% Success / 79.0% CP / +0.55 Delta Solution Length on TMDB and 72.7% Success / 74.5% CP / +0.25 on Spotify, outperforming the best baseline Reflexion (TMDB 52.0% Success / 59.0% CP; Spotify 59.6% / 61.4%) and ReAct (TMDB 44.0% / 57.0%; Spotify 54.5% / 49.1%), with the smallest Delta Solution Length (most efficient planning).
ablations: (1) Remove Planner (= ReAct equipped with the proposed executor): large drop to TMDB 44.0% Success / 57.0% CP, Spotify 54.5% / 49.1% - shows current LLMs cannot simultaneously plan, understand and select APIs, so the coarse-to-fine planner is the key driver. (2) Remove schema-based Parser (LLM directly parses raw JSON): drop to TMDB 46.0% Success / 53.0% CP, Spotify 47.3% / 52.7% - the OAS-schema-grounded code parser materially helps comprehension of complex responses. (3) Base-LLM swap: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) slightly worse than text-davinci-003 (TMDB 68.0% / 65.0%; Spotify 69.1% / 72.3%; ChatGPT over-plans/too verbose); Llama2-13B fails completely (0.0% on both, cannot follow the prompts); Vicuna-13B partially works (TMDB 9.0% / 15.0%; Spotify 12.7% / 20.6%). (4) Scaling analyses: success rate degrades with longer gold paths but RestGPT stays >40% at gold length 4 while all baselines collapse; adding noise APIs barely affects RestGPT while baselines deteriorate (robustness/extensibility). (5) Error breakdown: most errors arise in the planning stage (planner losing track / early exit, and API selector picking wrong APIs or hallucinating in-path parameters).
evaluation_decoupling: Partial: Correct Path rate is a path/selection-level (intrinsic-ish) metric reported separately from human-judged Success Rate (end-to-end outcome), and Delta Solution Length separately measures planning efficiency; the gap (CP slightly above Success) is interpreted as correct plans that fail at execution. However, no standalone retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are reported, since selection is LLM-driven rather than ranked.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both: outcome via human-judged Success Rate, plus process-level metrics - Correct Path rate (whether the intermediate API-call trajectory matches the gold solution path as a subsequence), Delta Solution Length (planning efficiency / extra calls), and a per-module error breakdown (planner vs API selector vs caller vs parser).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Planning efficiency reported via Delta Solution Length (extra API calls beyond gold): RestGPT is most efficient (TMDB +0.55, Spotify +0.25) vs e.g. Reflexion (+1.37 / +1.68) and Offline (+1.52 / +1.10); the case study shows RestGPT solving a task in 4 API calls vs ReAct's 6. Max generation length 256, temperature 0. No explicit dollar/API-cost, wall-clock latency, or token-count numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Variable, budget-driven selection rather than fixed-k: the API selector picks the one-or-few endpoints needed for the current sub-task; to respect the limited LLM context window the framework filters API docs so only endpoints in the current API plan a_t have their full OAS loaded into the caller (progressive disclosure). Generation capped at 256 tokens. The number of selected/called APIs per instruction is set by the plan (gold avg 2.3-2.6; RestGPT adds ~0.25-0.55 extra), not a preset k.
benchmark_construction_and_size: RestBench size: TMDB 54 APIs / 100 test + 10 dev instructions (gold path lengths 1-4, avg 2.3); Spotify 40 APIs / 57 test + 10 dev instructions (lengths 1-4, avg 2.6). Construction: bottom-up, human-curated - 6 NLP-expert annotators brainstorm realistic instructions over different API combinations and annotate gold API solution paths; 2 additional experts verify solvability and path correctness. Answer verifiability: API solution paths are largely stable so correctness is checked by gold-path-as-subsequence (Correct Path rate); because some instructions are time-dependent, final-answer success is judged by humans (Success Rate). Difficulty signal: best baselines reach only ~52-60% Success while all baselines fail at gold-path length 4; RestGPT reaches 72.7-75% Success and stays >40% at length 4.
builds_on: Coarse-to-fine online planning over an LLM agent built on LangChain (prompts inspired by the LangChain OpenAPI agent). Conceptually builds on ReAct (interleaved reasoning+acting), DEPS (interactive planning), Reflexion (feedback/reflection), and the offline plan-then-execute introspective method (Tool Learning with Foundation Models / HuggingGPT / Chameleon). Uses the OpenAPI Specification (Swagger) as the API-documentation standard and shares the autonomous-agent spirit of AutoGPT.
contrasts_with: Tool-augmented LLMs limited to a small set of specially-designed tools and inflexible planning: Toolformer, Visual ChatGPT, ViperGPT (offline program plans), HuggingGPT and Chameleon (offline natural-language plan-then-execute over fixed model/tool sets), API-Bank, GPT4Tools, and Gorilla (large API set but single-call, no online planning). RestGPT contrasts these with (a) standardized RESTful/OAS integration and plug-and-play extensibility to 100+ real APIs, and (b) an online coarse-to-fine plan-with-feedback loop instead of offline/static or pure-ReAct planning.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): an LLM-agent that selects and executes real-world RESTful API endpoints via online coarse-to-fine planning, with retrieval realized as LLM-as-retriever API selection over OAS endpoint descriptions and progressive-disclosure document loading. Sits between single-call API-grounding work (Gorilla) and large-scale tool-retrieval/agent benchmarks (API-Bank, ToolLLM/ToolBench, ToolRet); introduces RestBench as an early real-RESTful-API agent benchmark and emphasizes online planning + inter-API dependency handling over static tool retrieval.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: partial (LLM-as-retriever API selection over endpoint descriptions, not retrieval of prior solved cases), Reuse: no, Revise: partial (online re-planning via 'continue' feedback revises the plan, but not a retrieved case), Retain: no]. Not a case-based-reasoning system.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: the paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is a coarse-to-fine online planning tool-use agent over RESTful APIs.
